title: Finite locally constant sheaves and finite-etale schemes
statement:
For a scheme $T$, finite locally constant sheaves of sets on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$
are equivalent to finite etale $T$-schemes. A finite abelian group action on
the sheaf corresponds to an action by finite-etale $T$-automorphisms.

proof.text: For a finite etale $T$-scheme $P$, the local-trivializations node supplies its canonical sheaf of sections $h_P$, an etale cover, and finite sets $S_i$ with $h_P|_{U_i}\cong\underline{S_i}$. Thus $h_P$ is finite locally constant. Send a $T$-morphism $f:P\to Q$ to the natural transformation $h_f$ given on each section $x:V\to P$ by $x\mapsto f\circ x$. Associativity and identities make this assignment a functor $H$ into the full category of finite locally constant sheaves.

Let $E$ be finite locally constant. By the stated definition it is constant on an etale covering and its geometric stalks are finite, in particular at separably closed geometric points. Apply the representability node with exactly these hypotheses to obtain $P\to T$ finite etale and an isomorphism $h_P\cong E$. The node explicitly supplies an isomorphism of sheaves, so this is essential surjectivity of $H$; no extra connectedness, quasi-compactness, or fixed cardinality is needed.

Apply the Yoneda bijection in the category $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ to $P,Q$, which are objects since they are etale over $T$. Its morphisms between them are exactly $T$-morphisms. Because sheaves form a full subcategory of presheaves, the same bijection identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_T(P,Q)$ with sheaf morphisms $h_P\to h_Q$. Its inverse sends $\tau$ to $\tau_P(\mathrm{id}_P)$. Thus $H$ is full and faithful.

proof.text: Explicitly construct an inverse to $H$: for every $E$ choose a representative $P_E$ and $\epsilon_E:h_{P_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ as in step 2. For $u:E\to F$ let $G(u):P_E\to P_F$ be the unique morphism whose Yoneda image is $\epsilon_F^{-1}\circ u\circ\epsilon_E$. The bijection of step 3 proves $G(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $G(v\circ u)=G(v)\circ G(u)$, and makes $\epsilon:HG\cong\mathrm{id}$ natural. The unique morphism $\eta_P:P_{h_P}\to P$ mapping to $\epsilon_{h_P}$ is an isomorphism: the preimage of its inverse sheaf map is its inverse by injectivity. For $f:P\to Q$, the defining formula gives $H(G(H(f)))=\epsilon_{h_Q}^{-1}\circ H(f)\circ\epsilon_{h_P}$, whence $H(\eta_Q\circ G(H(f)))=H(f)\circ\epsilon_{h_P}=H(f\circ\eta_P)$. Injectivity proves $\eta_Q\circ G(H(f))=f\circ\eta_P$, so $\eta:GH\cong\mathrm{id}$ is natural. This proves the equivalence without invoking an uncited equivalence criterion.

source.place: Tag 03RV, explicit categorical assembly of object correspondence and Yoneda

proof.text: Let a finite abelian group $M$ act on $E$, meaning automorphisms $\rho_m$ with $\rho_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{m+n}=\rho_m\circ\rho_n$. For a representation $\epsilon:h_P\cong E$, define $a_m:P\to P$ as the unique preimage of $\epsilon^{-1}\circ\rho_m\circ\epsilon$ under step 3. Injectivity gives $a_0=\mathrm{id}$, $a_{m+n}=a_m\circ a_n$, and $a_{-m}$ inverse to $a_m$. These are $T$-automorphisms of the finite etale scheme. Conversely an action by $a_m$ induces $\rho_m=\epsilon\circ h_{a_m}\circ\epsilon^{-1}$, satisfying the same equations. The two assignments are inverse by the Yoneda bijection. For representations $\epsilon_E:h_P\cong E$ and $\epsilon_F:h_Q\cong F$, let $b:P\to Q$ represent $u:E\to F$. Then $u\circ\rho_m^E=\rho_m^F\circ u$ is equivalent, after composing with $\epsilon_F^{-1}$ and $\epsilon_E$, to $H(b)\circ H(a_m^P)=H(a_m^Q)\circ H(b)$, and injectivity makes this equivalent to $b\circ a_m^P=a_m^Q\circ b$. Thus the equivalence gives the claimed correspondence of actions, with no torsor or simple-transitivity assumption.
